title: Incident Type Metrics Labeling Proposal (v0.7) — allowlist + sampling + storage/cardinality impact
body:
Owner: Observability (Allison)
Last reviewed w/: SRE (Rafael), Dashboards (Sergio), SLO (Aisha), Data (Mei)

Context / why this doc exists
- Reliability Program is rolling out an incident taxonomy + required classification (incident_type + subtype + owner).
- We need metrics that support reporting: incident volume by type/owner, MTTA/MTTR, remediation SLA breach rate.
- We also want correlation from high-level symptom metrics (5xx/latency/streaming resets) to incident categories.
- Constraint: do NOT explode label cardinality on our hottest time series.

This proposal focuses on: metric schema changes, a label allowlist, sampling strategy, and impact estimate (storage + cardinality).


Goals
1) Make incident taxonomy measurable and auditable via metrics.
2) Provide stable, low-cardinality breakdowns by incident_type at org-level + tier-level.
3) Avoid blowing up Prometheus/remote-write costs or query latency.
4) Be explicit about what is allowed to be a label and where.

Non-goals
- Not deciding taxonomy itself (see Confluence: incident-taxonomy-v1-definitions).
- Not defining the incident-bot UX or enforcement rules (ENG-4822 / incident-bot PRs).
- Not solving “per-request classification” (an incident type is not known at request time in general).


Key observation (important)
Incident type is an incident-level attribute (set/updated by Incident Commander), not a request-level attribute.
Therefore, we should NOT attempt to add incident_type as a label to per-request counters/histograms like:
- http_requests_total
- request_latency_seconds_bucket
- tokens_generated_total
unless we’re very deliberate (sampling + aggregation) and/or only in low-volume derived metrics.


Proposed model: two-layer metrics
Layer A — Incident event metrics (authoritative for taxonomy reporting)
- Source of truth is incident-bot / incident service.
- Very low volume, safe to label with incident taxonomy.
- Used for: counts, MTTA/MTTR, remediation SLA compliance, owner attribution.

Layer B — Symptom + system health metrics (high volume)
- Existing request/infra metrics remain unchanged (or minimal changes).
- We JOIN/overlay taxonomy in dashboards by time window (incident timeline) rather than labeling every request.
- Used for: diagnostics during incident; trend baselines; correlating symptom spikes to incident windows.


Layer A: new/updated incident event metrics
(All emitted from incident-bot / incident events pipeline; 1–N events per incident)

1) redwood_incident_created_total (counter)
Labels (allowlist):
- incident_type (top-level only)
- incident_severity (sev0|sev1|sev2|sev3)
- customer_tier (hosted|dedicated|private)
- owner_team (resolved primary owner)
- region_group (optional; see below)

2) redwood_incident_milestone_seconds (gauge-like via histogram or event-based summary)
We need durations for: time-to-ack, time-to-mitigate, time-to-resolve, time-to-fix (policy-defined)
Option A (preferred): publish milestone events and compute in metrics pipeline
- redwood_incident_milestone_event_total
  Labels: milestone (created|acked|mitigated|resolved|fixed), incident_type, severity, tier, owner_team
Option B: direct duration histograms
- redwood_incident_tta_seconds_bucket
- redwood_incident_ttm_seconds_bucket
- redwood_incident_ttr_seconds_bucket
- redwood_incident_ttf_seconds_bucket
  Labels: incident_type, severity, tier, owner_team

3) redwood_incident_sla_breach_total (counter)
Labels:
- sla_kind (mitigation|fix)
- incident_type
- incident_severity
- customer_tier
- owner_team
- breach_reason (paused_force_majeure|customer_caused|unknown|not_paused)
Note: breach_reason is capped to a small enum.


Label allowlist (hard rules)
We propose an allowlist at instrumentation review + in the metrics pipeline.

Allowed taxonomy labels (Layer A only):
- incident_type: REQUIRED. Top-level category only.
- incident_subtype: DISALLOWED as a metric label for v1 (kept in logs/events; used in dashboards via sampled logs).
  Rationale: subtypes are the fastest-growing dimension and most likely to churn.
- owner_team: ALLOWED (primary only; single owner).
- customer_tier: ALLOWED (hosted|dedicated|private).
- incident_severity: ALLOWED.

Explicitly disallowed labels (both layers) due to cardinality and/or privacy:
- customer_id, org_id, workspace_id
- model_id / model_name (unless already part of a low-card metric and separately approved)
- route / endpoint / prompt template id
- incident_id (use exemplars / traces / logs instead)
- freeform text fields (root cause, summary, slack channel, etc.)

Region labeling guidance
- For Layer A, region can be useful but risky if we include full region + AZ + cluster.
- Proposal: allow a small region_group label, not raw region.
  region_group enum (example): us-east, us-west, eu, apac, unknown
- If we truly need raw region for certain reports, do it in logs or BigQuery-style analytics, not Prometheus.


Handling unknown/unclassified
We need stable buckets so dashboards don’t break and so compliance is measurable.
- incident_type MUST be set to a value.
- Allowed fallback buckets:
  - incident_type=unknown (used for first 15 minutes if IC hasn’t classified yet)
  - incident_type=other (last resort; requires postmortem follow-up to reclassify)
- We will track compliance explicitly:
  - redwood_incident_unclassified_total (counter)
    Labels: customer_tier, severity, owner_team (owner_team may be “unresolved”)


Layer B: symptom metrics changes (minimal)
We should not add incident_type to request metrics.
Instead:
1) Alert payloads include incident_type when known (ENG-4823), and dashboards overlay incident windows.
2) For a few coarse “alert-level” derived metrics (not per request), we can add incident_type safely.

Proposed derived/alert-level metrics (low volume):
- redwood_alert_fired_total
  Labels: alert_name (allowlisted), incident_type (when attached), severity, tier, owner_team
- redwood_alert_to_incident_linked_total
  Labels: alert_name, incident_type, severity, tier

What we do NOT change in v1
- No incident_type label on: request_errors_total, request_latency histograms, token counters.
- No incident_subtype in Prometheus.


Sampling strategy (where it applies)
Sampling is relevant for any metric/log stream that could explode:
- We avoid adding labels to high-volume metrics entirely (preferred).
- For logs-based analytics used for subtype drilldowns:
  - keep subtype in structured logs/events
  - sample at ingestion for high-volume components (e.g., per-request gateway logs)
  - do NOT sample Layer A incident event metrics

Proposed sampling defaults
- Incident event stream: 100% (expected low volume)
- Alert event stream: 100% (still low-ish; depends on flappy alerts)
- Request logs with subtype hints: 1% baseline, burst to 5% during incident windows
  (burst controlled by incident-bot emitting a “diagnostic sampling on” annotation)


Cardinality + storage impact estimate (back-of-envelope)
Assumptions (based on recent quarters; Mei to validate with backfill):
- ~250–450 incidents / quarter org-wide (including internal high-sev)
- Active incident concurrency rarely > 3–5
- Top-level incident_type categories in v1: target 10–15
- owner_team: ~8–12 core eng teams
- customer_tier: 3
- severity: 4

Layer A expected time series
If we publish counters with labels (type * owner * tier * severity):
- 15 * 12 * 3 * 4 = 2,160 series per metric
Multiply by:
- created_total (1)
- milestone_event_total (1, but milestone label adds ~5 values)
- sla_breach_total (1, sla_kind adds 2 values)
Rough total:
- created_total: ~2.2k
- milestone_event_total: ~2.2k * 5 milestones = ~10.8k
- sla_breach_total: ~2.2k * 2 = ~4.3k
Total incremental series: ~17–20k series
This is acceptable in Prometheus/remote-write as long as we keep it isolated from hot request metrics.

Why subtype is excluded (numbers get ugly fast)
If subtype count grows to even 40 values:
- 15 types * 40 subtypes (if modeled separately) * 12 owners * 3 tiers * 4 severities
  => 86,400+ series per metric, before milestones
That’s not acceptable for v1.

Storage estimate (very rough)
- Incident event counters are sparse (few samples per minute) compared to request metrics.
- Even 20k additional series is typically fine if scrape interval is 30–60s and churn is low.
- Risk is mostly query UX + label churn (e.g., owners changing, types renamed).
Mitigation: enforce enums in pipeline + versioned allowlist.


Implementation plan (proposed)
Phase 0: Guardrails first (this doc)
- Define allowlist + disallow list.
- Add CI/lint in observability-pack for “no new labels without review”.

Phase 1: Emit Layer A incident metrics
- Update incident-bot / incident service to emit created + milestone events with required labels.
- Ensure owner_team is resolved via control-plane mapping config (ENG-4825).

Phase 2: Dashboards + reporting
- Sergio to implement dashboards in observability-pack using Layer A metrics.
- Add a panel explicitly showing “unknown/other” usage.

Phase 3 (optional): Diagnostic sampling + subtype drilldowns
- Add logs/events pipeline queries for subtype-level analysis (not in Prometheus).
- Use incident windows to scope queries.


Open questions / decisions needed
1) Where do incident event metrics live?
- Option A: incident-bot emits to metrics gateway.
- Option B: control plane incident service emits to our standard OTel collector.
Preference: B for consistency + auth/audit.

2) owner_team labeling source
- Use resolved primary owner at incident close? or at creation time?
Proposed: emit both as fields in events, but only label primary_owner_current (single label).
If ownership changes mid-incident, emit an owner_changed milestone event (and keep labels stable per sample).

3) tier definition for internal incidents
- Some incidents are “internal reliability risk” without clear customer tier.
Proposal: customer_tier=internal for Layer A (adds 1 value; still ok).
Need agreement from SRE/Program.

4) Region labeling
- Keep region_group only? or allow raw region on incident events?
Observability recommendation: region_group only in v1.


Appendix: Proposed allowlisted enums (draft)
incident_type (top-level) — examples only (final list owned by SRE taxonomy doc)
- availability_error_rate
- latency_regression
- streaming_disconnects
- routing_fallback_misbehavior
- capacity_fleet_shortage
- control_plane_outage
- auth_rbac_failure
- telemetry_blind_spot
- private_connectivity_config
- other
- unknown

owner_team (examples)
- eng-sre
- eng-observability
- eng-platform-control-plane
- eng-platform-routing
- eng-infra-fleet
- eng-serving-runtime
- security-ops
- eng-private-deployments

milestone
- created
- acked
- mitigated
- resolved
- fixed


Notes / action items
- Allison: sync with Rafael on whether we need customer_tier=internal (and how it impacts SLA policy evaluator).
- Mei: validate incident volume assumptions from last 2 quarters + estimate incident_type distribution.
- Sergio: confirm dashboard queries work well with milestone_event_total approach.
- Dylan/Tooling: confirm incident-bot can emit milestone events reliably (avoid duplicates; idempotency key needed).

(End)
